messages:
maria: FYI p99 for hosted-api spiked ~20:02 UTC, from ~450ms -> ~1.8s for ~8 minutes. Alerts firing. Looks like one tenant burst but curious about runtime behavior (queue depth, kernel fallbacks, kvcache).
ken: Confirming. Grafana shows queue depth on runtime-pool-a up to 220-260 per worker, request backlog causing higher latency. p95 bumped too but not as high as p99.
infra-bot: [ALERT] hosted-api.p99 > 1.5s for 5m (sustained) — check runtime pool and rate limiter.
devon: Pasted a quick runtime profile from one busy shard:```kernel_selector: fallback_count=184, preferred_count=420
batch_size_dist: {1: 62%, 2: 18%, 4+: 20%}
kv_cache: miss_rate=32%, eviction/sec=48, rewarm_events=7```Looks like lots of single-request batches + kvcache thrash.
sophie: I also pulled runtime logs. Kernel selector logged sequence-length mismatches and used slower matmul_fallback for ~14% of requests in the spike window. Suspect recent heuristic change that tries to avoid small-*fast* kernels when shape variance present.
dave: KV cache metrics show TTL churn — a tenant flooded with diverse prompts causing cache fragmentation. Misses jump from 5% baseline to 30% during the window. That increases token compute and KV IO, amplifying latency.
ken: Note we rolled kernel-selector tweak in rollout yesterday (canary -> prod). Could be a regression where mismatched seq lengths now prefer fallback kernel more often. Also batching heuristic stats match: singletons are high which kills throughput.
maria: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) throttle noisy tenant at gateway (soft cap) 2) flip kernel-selector to prior heuristic on a small canary set 3) force kvcache rewarm/evict policy back to conservative 4) monitor p99 and queue depth. Who can run the flips? @sophie @devon
sophie: On it — I'll update canary via: `kubectl set env deploy/runtime KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy-heuristic --namespace=prod-canary` and watch.
devon: I can toggle kvcache policy. Changing `KV_EVICTION_WINDOW=60s` -> `300s` to reduce churn. Applying to canaries now.
ken: I'll add a temporary tenant throttle at the gateway: `rate-limit: tenant: T-12345 -> 100r/s` and enable preferential routing away from shared pool.
deploy-bot: Deployment roll triggered: runtime@canary -> set KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy-heuristic by sophie.
infra-bot: Rollback candidate detected for kernel-selector v2.4 -> scheduling canary rollback to 3 nodes.
dave: Quick check: after toggles on canary for ~90s, p99 on canary nodes dropped from 1.8s -> 520ms, queue depth halved. Baseline nodes still higher until throttle applied.
maria: Good. Keep throttles until we validate. Action items: - sophie/deploy: canary flip (done) - devon: kvcache policy change (done) - ken: gateway throttle (in progress) - dave: continue monitoring eviction metrics.
sophie: FYI logs show fewer `matmul_fallback` occurrences after flip.
ken: Gateway throttle applied. Noisy tenant now at 80r/s rolling cap. Global queue depth trending down.
infra-bot: Alert cleared: hosted-api.p99 < 0.6s for 3m on canary.
maria: Thanks — keeping this thread open for 30m to watch for regressions. If stable, we'll schedule a rollback of the selector patch and write a postmortem with kernel-selector A/B perf numbers and kvcache tuning notes. :thumbsup:
devon: I'll collect profiling artifacts (pprof, kernel traces, batch histograms) and upload to the incident bucket.
dave: Final quick note — add a histogram alarm for batch_size singleton ratio >50% so we catch similar patterns earlier.
maria: Agreed. Closing once postmortem draft is ready.
